Specify a fitting backend for xplus

Source: R/backends.R
xplus_backend.Rd

Describe a learner that xplus() uses for both the iterative pseudo-labeling fits and the final model. Built-in backends are xplus_backend_glmnet(), xplus_backend_ranger(), xplus_backend_gam(), xplus_backend_xgboost(), and xplus_backend_lightgbm(); this constructor defines custom learners with the same contract.

Usage

xplus_backend(
  name,
  fit,
  predict,
  importance = NULL,
  label = name,
  uses_cv = FALSE,
  parameters = NULL,
  fit_predict = NULL,
  supports_fractional = TRUE,
  supports_weights = TRUE
)

Arguments

name

Nonempty character scalar identifying the backend.

fit

Function with signature fit(x, y, foldid, weights) returning a fitted model object. x is the finite numeric feature matrix, y a numeric target in [0, 1] (binary during iterations, possibly fractional in the final fit), foldid the stratified cross-validation fold assignment, and weights nonnegative case weights encoding bootstrap multiplicities. To report a cross-validation measure in the iteration history, attach attr(model, "xplus_cv_measure") with "deviance" or "auc"; otherwise "none" is recorded.

predict

Function with signature predict(model, newx) returning finite probabilities in [0, 1], one per row of newx.

importance

Optional function with signature importance(model) returning a named numeric vector of feature scores, or NULL.

label

Human-readable backend label; defaults to name.

uses_cv

Logical scalar; whether fit performs internal cross-validation whose measure is recorded in the iteration history.

parameters

Optional data frame declaring tunable hyperparameters following the caret modelInfo convention (columns parameter, class, and label); informational only, it enables future tuning and AutoML adapters without changing the backend contract.

fit_predict

Optional function with signature fit_predict(model, x) returning honest probabilities for the rows passed to fit, in the same order — out-of-bag or held-out-fold estimates rather than in-sample memorization. xplus() uses them after the final fit for cutoff calibration and the stored training predictions; non-finite entries fall back to predict on those rows. When NULL, predict is reused on training rows, appropriate for learners that do not memorize per-observation targets. Iterative pseudo-label fits always use predict, which keeps self-training dynamics uniform across backends.

supports_fractional

Logical scalar; whether fit handles fractional targets in [0, 1] (the final pseudo-label fit). When FALSE, xplus() fails with a clear error if the final targets are non-binary instead of surfacing an engine-specific error deep in the learner.

supports_weights

Logical scalar; whether fit honors case weights. When FALSE, xplus() warns once that sampling = "bootstrap" multiplicities will be silently ignored by this learner.

Value

An object of class "xplus_backend" accepted by the backend argument of xplus().

Details

The contract mirrors the minimal estimator interface shared by caret modelInfo entries, sklearn fit/predict_proba estimators (the basis of PU wrappers such as ElkanotoPuClassifier), and mlr3 Learner objects: fit weighted (x, y) data, then predict probabilities. xplus additionally supplies foldid (stratified CV folds for backends that use them) and soft fractional targets in the final fit, which generic frameworks do not provide.

See also

xplus(), xplus_backend_ranger(), xplus_backend_gam()

Examples

constant <- xplus_backend(
  name = "constant",
  fit = function(x, y, foldid, weights) stats::weighted.mean(y, weights),
  predict = function(model, newx) rep(model, nrow(newx))
)
fit <- xplus(matrix(rnorm(100 * 5), ncol = 5), c(rep(1, 20), rep(0, 80)),
  backend = constant, max_iter = 3)
